simple.meaning: הַמְנִיךְ (hamnîyk) is a Hebrew word meaning “a necklace.” BibleIQ connects the English word back to this source word so its use can be compared across Scripture.
simple.biblicalBackground: הַמְנִיךְ (H2002) appears 6 times in the Hebrew Bible, beginning at Daniel 5:7, with occurrences in Daniel.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to הַמְנִיךְ (H2002) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: English translations can use the same English word for different Hebrew words. BibleIQ anchors the study in הַמְנִיךְ (H2002) before moving outward to related references.
simple.summary: הַמְנִיךְ (hamnîyk) / H2002 is traced through Daniel 5:7, Daniel 5:16, Daniel 5:29 using source-language evidence and occurrence comparison.

firstOccurrence.englishText: The king cried aloud to bring in the enchanters, the Chaldeans, and the soothsayers. The king spoke and said to the wise men of Babylon, “Whoever reads this writing, and shows me its interpretation, shall be clothed with purple, and have a chain of gold about his neck, and shall be the third ruler in the kingdom.”

definitions.full: H2002. hamnika הַמְנִיכָא Qr (Kt המינכָא , also [Gi] המוניכא , etc.) noun [masculine] chain, necklace (Talmud הַמְנִכָּא D WB 108 ; Syriac ; loan-word from Greek μανιάκης K § 64, 4 ; or < Persian hämy¹n , girdle [diminutive would be hamy¹nak ] (whence also Greek μαν ., Bev Dr Dan 5:7 ) Andr M 60* (reading הַמְיָֽנְכָא ); see also Behrm ix Lag Ges. Abh. 40; Arm. Stud. 1420 ; see Krauss 5f. (who compares also Talmud מָנְיָיק מוּנְיָיק, necklace, bracelet , Levy NHWB iii. 52 b, 158 b D 230 )); — of gold, 5:7 , 16 , 29 .
definitions.rootNote: (Aramaic) but the text is הֲמוּנֵךְ ; of foreign origin;
